Instrument (EN): Birth Satisfaction Scale-Revised — Russian validated postpartum edition
Scales / measured domains (EN): Stress experienced during labour (4); Women's personal attributes (2); Quality of care provision (4); total birth satisfaction
Research provenance: Zakharov S et al., Journal of Reproductive and Infant Psychology, published online 2026-03-20, DOI 10.1080/02646838.2026.2646667. Russian-language maternal participants n=223; forward/backward translation and cognitive pretest; CFA three/two/bifactor adequate, one-factor poor; alpha .71 stress/.70 attributes/.77 quality/.84 total, omega total .85.
DB locales: Not registered in published Supabase app.assessment_versions; similar substring BSS unrelated Barber Suggestibility Scale / body shame.
EN form: EN: Original English BSS-R exists and is described by developer; not newly EN-validated in this study.
RU form: RU-RU: translated, adapted and psychometrically studied in 223 Russian-speaking postpartum women; 2026 new Russian respondent edition.
ES form: ES: Earlier Spanish BSS-R validated independently, but this study did NOT validate Spanish or add Spanish translation.
Other translations: Other developer-listed translations include PT, TR, IT etc; no new validation assessed here.
Target population: Russian-speaking postpartum women N223, online cross-sectional survey; not designed as general mental-health screen.
Commercial digital use / permission revi: Copyright jointly held by C.J. Hollins Martin and C.R. Martin. Developer official BSS-R site states free for research/clinical use ONLY after permission; proprietary digital commercial hosting of RU wording, automated scoring and adaptation requires specific written permission; article CC BY is not questionnaire license.
Verification notes / safety gate: RESEARCH_ONLY. Clinical/perinatal boundaries; exact authorized RU respondent copy and scoring not received; no diagnostic cutoffs, display or deployment.

Instrument (EN): Intuitive Eating Scale-3 — Brazilian Portuguese 12-item adult validation
Scales / measured domains (EN): Unconditional permission to eat; Eating for physical rather than emotional reasons; Reliance on internal hunger/satiety cues; Body-food choice congruence; general intuitive eating
Research provenance: Carvalho PHB et al., Eating Disorders, published online 2026-10-16; DOI 10.1080/10640266.2026.2746538. N522 Brazilian adults, split sample EFA N254 and CFA remaining participants; 4-factor/bifactor structure and full gender invariance; study supports reliability of total and four subscales.
DB locales: No IES-3 PT-BR assessment published in app.assessment_versions. Master already has IES-3 original EN-US12 and TR12; THIS is new PT-BR edition evidence, not a new parent instrument.
EN form: EN: Original IES-3 12-item developer form (Tylka et al., 2024); 2026 Brazilian study does not validate English form.
RU form: RU: No independently validated RU respondent version evidenced by study.
ES form: ES: No independently validated ES respondent version evidenced by study.
Other translations: PT-BR: Brazilian Portuguese translated participant scale psychometrically studied among N522 adult men and women.
Target population: Brazilian men and women N522, general adult population; not an eating-disorder diagnosis.
Commercial digital use / permission revi: Original IES-3 developer handbook (Cambridge 2025) explicitly says original measure free to use in any setting, but commercial online redistribution of Brazilian translated items, version authorization and attribution need rights-holder confirmation; do not infer article license covers translated form.
Verification notes / safety gate: RESEARCH_ONLY. Sex invariance in one Brazilian adult sample not generalization to adolescents or clinical eating disorders; exact PT-BR wording and scoring/version permissions pending; no clinical cutoffs.

Instrument (EN): Closure and Resolution Scale — original event-resolution measure
Scales / measured domains (EN): Finality; Understanding; Felt distance; Emotional relief; Mental release; Behavioural deactivation (six factors)
Research provenance: Boucher CM, Scoboria A, Soucie K, Pascual-Leone A; Memory, online 2024-11-19, print 2025 33(2):205–222, DOI 10.1080/09658211.2024.2427666. Original EFA N284, revised EFA N158, separate CFA N159, convergent/discriminant N182; North-American mostly educated samples; psychometric evidence preliminary.
DB locales: No CRS key or event-closure scale published in active Supabase; distinguish from need-for-emotional-closure (NECS) and generic clinical outcome measures.
EN form: EN: Original English-language North American developer research; exact finalized respondent prompts not independently retrieved or cleared; NOT a translated edition.
RU form: RU: No RU respondent translation/psychometric validation established.
ES form: ES: No ES respondent translation/psychometric validation established.
Other translations: No other independently validated respondent language edition identified.
Target population: North American community/adult samples in four reported stages N284, 158, 159, 182; predominantly White and postsecondary education.
Commercial digital use / permission revi: Academic article and journal copyright do NOT establish rights to reproduce 34 final respondent items or electronically score them in a fee-based service. Request author/rightsholder permission and final form/scoring documentation.
Verification notes / safety gate: RESEARCH_ONLY. Measure captures perceived resolution of personally significant past events, not diagnosis or effectiveness of psychotherapy; early evidence, replication in clinical/other language groups required.
